title: Earth and Planetary Systems Intelligence — Research Domain Catalog

policy.purpose: Register separate research domains that share evidence-ingestion, provenance, uncertainty and review infrastructure without forcing their scientific targets into one model or score.
common_rules: Missing observations remain unknown; they are not automatically negative evidence.
Observations, derived products, model outputs and expert hypotheses have distinct evidence types.
Products sharing the same upstream observation are not independent corroboration.
Predictions must state spatial and temporal support, coverage, uncertainty, domain of validity and known failure modes.
A high score is a screening hypothesis, not ground truth, a causal claim, or an operational instruction.
Dataset access, license, attribution and redistribution permissions are checked per artifact and layer.
Local communities, land rights, permits, ecological safeguards and human priorities constrain action; they are not optional score weights.

architecture.sol_atlas: Spatial and temporal presentation, evidence-layer toggles, coverage and dissent views.
architecture.symthaea: Generate and compare explicit hypotheses, detect contradictions, and propose discriminating observations; never act as authoritative evidence.
architecture.mycelix: Bind claims to immutable dataset/artifact digests, provenance, consent/access constraints, review attestations and supersession history.
architecture.symtropy: Run only domain-appropriate, validated scenario simulations; do not substitute its current generic rigid-body physics for geoscience, hydrology or climate solvers.

policy.acceptance_rule: A domain remains candidate research until its data rights, metadata, reproducible baseline, domain-appropriate validation, uncertainty report, failure analysis and independent review gates are satisfied.

domains.title: Mineral systems and geological resources
domains.question: Where should additional geological investigation be prioritized for a specified mineral system, given spatially incomplete and differently resolved evidence?
domains.scope: Deposit-type-specific prospectivity using geology, geophysics, geochemistry, remote sensing where appropriate, and tectonic context only when relevant.

data_sources.name: South African consensus-based prospectivity benchmark
data_sources.provider: Nwaila et al. / Natural Resources Research
data_sources.role: Primary reproducibility benchmark for PGE–Ni–Cu–Cr and Witwatersrand-type Au.
key_limitations: Supporting material is a large supplementary PDF and has not been extracted in this work.
Unlabeled areas are not equivalent to confirmed barren ground.

data_sources.name: Compilation of geospatial data for mineral industries and related infrastructure in Africa
data_sources.role: Data-ingestion smoke test and regional context; not ground truth for modelled undiscovered tracts.
key_limitations: Component-layer metadata and source ancestry need review.
Some layers are existing assessments and would create leakage if treated as independent labels.

prohibited_inferences: A prospectivity score proves an economic deposit.
Satellite data directly resolve deep ore bodies.
A modeled undiscovered-resource tract is independent ground truth.

validation.split_strategy: Grouped spatial holdouts by district, deposit cluster or geological unit; temporal backtests only when source dates permit.
metrics: recall within top 1/5/10 percent of eligible area

domains.title: Water security, drought and water-storage change
domains.question: Where are water-storage, soil-moisture or drought indicators changing, and which local measurements would distinguish climate variability from local abstraction or infrastructure problems?
domains.scope: Combine satellite-supported water-storage indicators with precipitation, soil moisture, hydrography, reservoir observations, aquifer maps and local measurements when available.

data_sources.name: GRACE and GRACE-FO groundwater and soil-moisture drought indicators
data_sources.role: Regional water-storage and model-assimilated groundwater/soil-moisture drought indicators.
key_limitations: Global product is coarse (about 0.25-degree grid).
Indicators are model-assimilated and do not directly identify individual wells or local aquifer depletion caused by pumping.

data_sources.name: WaPOR remote-sensing data for water productivity
data_sources.role: Water and land productivity variables for agriculture across Africa and the Near East.
key_limitations: Coverage and variable resolution differ by WaPOR level and product.
Water productivity is not a direct measure of household access, water quality or groundwater reserves.

required_checks: compare with gauges/wells/reservoir records when available
separate climate variability from pumping attribution
prohibited_inferences: Coarse GRACE grids identify an individual depleted well.
Drought correlation proves groundwater over-abstraction.
Agricultural water productivity equals safe drinking-water access.

validation.split_strategy: Hold out basins or regions and test time periods not used to tune thresholds; compare against appropriate in-situ records when available.
metrics: detection lead time where forecast is explicitly evaluated

domains.title: Agricultural productivity and land-water management
domains.question: Where do crop and land-water productivity indicators deteriorate, where are they improving, and what local evidence would identify the responsible process?
domains.scope: Monitor land-cover context, rainfall, evapotranspiration and water productivity. Crop-type and yield inference requires crop calendars, ground observations and locally validated models.
target_geography: global only where input products support it

data_sources.name: WaPOR remote-sensing data for water productivity
data_sources.role: Core Africa/Near East land and water productivity observations and derived products.
key_limitations: Coverage and spatial resolution vary by level.
A derived productivity layer does not uniquely identify agronomic cause.

data_sources.name: ESA WorldCover
data_sources.role: Land-cover and land-use context.
key_limitations: 2020 v100 and 2021 v200 use different algorithm versions; naive differencing confounds real change with algorithm change.
Nominal 10 m products do not make every downstream estimate 10 m accurate.

data_sources.name: Global Precipitation Measurement data
data_sources.role: Precipitation context across seasons and extreme rainfall events.
key_limitations: Products vary in latency, grid, algorithm and sensor combination.
Rainfall alone does not determine crop yield or soil-water availability.

prohibited_inferences: Remote sensing alone proves crop yield, food availability or farmer intent.
A difference between WorldCover versions is necessarily land-cover change.
A productivity anomaly identifies its cause without corroborating evidence.

validation.split_strategy: Hold out agricultural regions and seasons; test across crop/ecological zones rather than random neighboring pixels.
metrics: calibration by crop/zone where ground truth exists

domains.title: Ecosystems, restoration and carbon stocks
domains.question: Where is land cover or vegetation structure changing, and where would field ecology be most valuable to distinguish degradation, recovery and natural variability?
domains.scope: Map land-cover context, forest structure and biomass proxies. Carbon-stock estimates and restoration success require product-specific uncertainty and suitable field or inventory validation.

data_sources.name: ESA WorldCover
data_sources.role: Land-cover context at nominal 10 m resolution.
key_limitations: Different algorithm versions in 2020 and 2021 mean naive pixelwise difference is not a pure change product.
Class and geography-specific accuracy must be consulted.

data_sources.name: Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI)
data_sources.role: Lidar-derived vegetation structure and biomass-related observations/products.
key_limitations: GEDI observations are footprint-based and mission/product coverage varies; gridded products aggregate sparse lidar sampling.
Biomass is not a complete measure of biodiversity or ecosystem condition.

data_sources.name: Global Forest Watch data API
data_sources.provider: World Resources Institute / Global Forest Watch
data_sources.role: Additional forest-change dataset discovery and queries where terms and API access permit.
key_limitations: API authentication and dataset versions matter.
Forest loss products do not alone establish illegality, ecological outcome or local consent.

prohibited_inferences: A vegetation index alone proves biodiversity or restoration success.
Aboveground biomass equals total ecosystem carbon.
A forest-loss alert proves illegality or identifies a responsible person.

validation.split_strategy: Hold out landscapes and years; compare to independent plots, inventories or field assessments.
metrics: performance by biome and canopy type
false-change rate caused by algorithms or seasonality

domains.title: Wildfire, flood, rainfall extremes and drought monitoring
domains.question: Where are hazards developing or impacts accumulating, what is the observation latency, and which independent source can confirm the signal?
domains.scope: Monitoring and retrospective validation first; forecasts only when an independently evaluated forecast model and uncertainty are explicitly supplied.
target_geography: South Africa and Southern Africa first

data_sources.name: Fire Information for Resource Management System
data_sources.role: Satellite active-fire detections and web-service distribution.
key_limitations: Active-fire pixels are detections, not a perfect fire perimeter or proof of cause.
Sensor, product version and latency are material; the API page currently announces a Suomi NPP product transition effective 1 November 2026.

data_sources.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service data
data_sources.role: Drought, flood and emergency mapping products where geography and activation coverage apply.
key_limitations: Some products are regional, event-triggered or service-specific rather than uniform global observations.
Map availability and publication time differ from event time.

data_sources.name: Global Precipitation Measurement data
data_sources.role: Rainfall context for hydrometeorological extremes.
key_limitations: Precipitation estimates have product-dependent resolution, latency and uncertainty.
Rainfall intensity alone does not equal local flood impact.

required_checks: event time vs observation time vs publication time
prohibited_inferences: A hotspot detection is a confirmed perimeter or fire cause.
A near-real-time observation is a forecast.
Absence of a detection means no hazard.

validation.split_strategy: Event-based holdouts across seasons/regions; never split neighboring detections from the same event between train and test.

domains.title: Renewable energy and low-carbon infrastructure screening
domains.question: Where may solar, wind or other energy projects merit a feasibility study when resource quality, demand, grid access, land use, ecology, water and community constraints are considered together?
domains.scope: Pre-feasibility screening only; site-level decisions require validated resource measurements, engineering studies, grid capacity, land/permit checks and community process.
target_geography: other regions when input data and rules are suitable

data_sources.name: Global Solar Atlas
data_sources.provider: World Bank / ESMAP and technical partners
data_sources.role: Solar-resource screening and map context.
key_limitations: Map-derived resource estimates are not a substitute for site measurements or bankable yield assessment.
Grid, land, ecology, water and social constraints require separate evidence.

data_sources.name: Copernicus Data Space catalogue
data_sources.role: Land-cover and Earth-observation context where appropriate.
key_limitations: Sensor products have different spatial/temporal support, processing levels and masking needs.
A satellite image does not reveal grid hosting capacity.

data_sources.name: OpenStreetMap data
data_sources.role: Infrastructure and accessibility context.
key_limitations: Coverage/completeness varies geographically and by feature type.
ODbL attribution and share-alike obligations need careful review for derived databases.

prohibited_inferences: Best solar resource alone means best build site.
OpenStreetMap infrastructure coverage is complete.
A ranked site is permitted, feasible or socially accepted.

validation.split_strategy: Compare known operational projects and held-out regions; evaluate against measured resource/production where available.

domains.title: Infrastructure resilience and access to essential services
domains.question: Which areas may be poorly connected to essential services or exposed to infrastructure disruption, and which local records should be checked first?
domains.scope: Aggregate accessibility and exposure estimates using public roads, settlements, population surfaces and authoritative service locations where permitted. No individual surveillance or sensitive-person inference.
target_geography: other regions where source data support it

data_sources.name: OpenStreetMap data
data_sources.role: Road and mapped facility context.
key_limitations: Mapped roads/facilities may be incomplete or out of date.
ODbL terms must be considered for derived databases.

data_sources.name: Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL)
data_sources.role: Settlement and built-up context at product-specific temporal/spatial resolution.
key_limitations: Gridded population/settlement data are estimates, not a census of every household.
Product epochs and modeling assumptions differ.

required_checks: uncertainty in population and road coverage
prohibited_inferences: A mapped gap proves an essential service is absent.
Population surfaces identify specific people or households.
A model may determine aid eligibility without accountable local review.

validation.split_strategy: Hold out municipalities/districts and compare against independent service inventories, travel times or surveys.

domains.title: Circular materials, secondary resources and industrial waste
domains.question: Where might documented industrial by-products, tailings or end-of-life materials be recoverable or reused, and what evidence is needed to assess safety and material composition?
domains.scope: Join reported facilities, waste inventories, material-flow data, assays and regulatory records where available. Remote sensing can show landform/change but cannot alone determine composition, toxicity or recoverability.

data_sources.name: USGS Africa mineral-industries geodatabase
data_sources.role: Mining, processing and exploration context where source layers are appropriate.
key_limitations: Not a complete registry of tailings, waste chemistry or recycling facilities.
Existing resource assessments must not be treated as measured recoverable material.

prohibited_inferences: A visible tailings feature reveals chemical composition.
Recorded mass equals economically or environmentally recoverable material.
Modelled value overrides safety and permitting.

validation.split_strategy: Site-by-site cross-checks against independent inventories and laboratory/assay results; scenario assumptions stress-tested.

domains.title: Planetary surfaces and comparative geology
domains.question: What do mapped geology, topography, morphology and spectral observations suggest about surface processes on the Moon, Mars and other bodies?
domains.scope: Separate planetary bodies, coordinate reference systems, projections, sensor calibrations and geological priors. Start with published maps and calibrated data; do not port Earth-specific models without validation.
target_geography: other bodies where data and models support the question

data_sources.name: NASA Planetary Data System
data_sources.role: Archive of spacecraft, mission, ground-based and laboratory planetary science data.
key_limitations: Calibration, coordinate frames, projection, mission timing and product documentation are mission-specific.
Archive availability does not make all product processing or scientific interpretations equivalent.

data_sources.name: USGS planetary geologic maps and analysis-ready data
data_sources.role: Published planetary geologic maps, GIS resources and selected analysis-ready data.
key_limitations: Map scale and positional accuracy vary by body/product; some published maps are coarse for local exploration.
Earth grid assumptions, sea-level datums and coordinate semantics do not transfer directly.

prohibited_inferences: Earth-trained geology model transfers unmodified to the Moon/Mars.
A spectral signature uniquely establishes mineralogy without calibration/context.
A resource proxy establishes technical/economic extraction feasibility.

validation.split_strategy: Hold out mapped regions, mission observations or bodies where legitimate; validate against published maps and independent calibrated measurements.
